item.content:encoded:
I wrote this SCP in 2008. (I am also the original writer of 722)

For the record: I appreciate the revisions to this over my original version, and I don't want to seem like I am taking credit for someone's very good work. We were kind of just writing pulpy bullshit back then and there just wasn't that much care being taken with respect to cultural accuracy, which was a mistake. The tone and quality of writing needed to be improved and the cultural dressing I clumsily and disrespectfully pasted into the story was a distraction from what it was really supposed to be about anyway.

For a little history: When this whole thing got started, there was a constant flow of absolute trash trying to fit into the 666 spot. I think six or seven entries (or more) got rejected, with the absolute worst two being, respectively: A spooky TV that only plays Jesus being tortured, and Literally Damien from The Omen. It was basically understood that any overt reference to satan was probably going to be rejected and everyone was tired of seeing them.

I wrote 666 during a late shift at a call center while I was going through some shit with my dad, who was a recently relapsed addict. Temptation as a metaphor for the (conceptual) devil and how it intersects with addiction was the most compelling take I could think of that would satisfy both the "It can't just be scifi crap" people and the "it can't be religious crap" people. A space that manipulates addicts into use and relapse was uniquely horrifying to me, and still is. I lost my dad about six months after I wrote this.

item.title: a bit dissappointing
item.content:encoded:
The SCP is a great idea. but the execution of the story is a bit lacking. I would have expected a more in depth examination of its properties, or a broader sample of experiments to determine how it works. As a side note to this, it seems that the SCP is generally concerned and wants people to get better. However it leaves a lot of questions.

The anomalous nature of it is wonderfully crafted. How the entity inside refuses to answer questions. However, the only experiment described leaves the reader wanting more than just the one off explanation that if it finds you unworthy it kills you quickly.

This SCP seems more like it would try at least twice before killing the person inside. The way the description of it reads is that it progressively gets more violent, not just suddenly turns that way and attempts to kill the test subject.

A final point, it would have been nice to see the log of an experiment where the test subject succeeded in giving up their addiction. This would show both sides of the entity inside the SCP.
